subject: Hierarchical beta-binomial to estimate measure of risk

messages.author: 7256a40312b62f90
messages.subject: Hierarchical beta-binomial to estimate measure of risk
parts:
Hi,
I am new to STAN and relatively new to Bayesian stats, but very excited about its application.
We have survey data from floatplane pilots showing 727 destination lakes (j = 1 ... 727). For each j- destination we have:
- total number of pilots flying to j
- total number of pilots arriving at j from infested source lakes
- total number of flights arriving at j
- total number of flights to j originating at infested source lakes

I set up a beta-binomial hierarchical model adapted from the rat example in Carpenter et al. 2016 "Stan: A probabilistic programming language ...",  p.16
The objective is to get a marginal probability distribution for a measure of risk for each of the 727 destination lakes. The code below works great with results as expected.
To meet the assumption of independence in the binomial, I had to choose the proportion of pilots from source lakes as the measure of risk (tumor rate). However, a better measure of risk in my case would be the proportion of flights from source lakes. Risk of invasion is greater the larger the number of flights from source lakes. Yet flights violate the assumption of independence in the binomial. 

Question:
Is anybody aware of a hierarchical approach that would estimate the credible intervals using the number of pilots as the sample size, while using the proportion of flights as the measure of risk (theta)? 

Thank you very much for your help!

Tobias


data {
  int<lower=0> J; // number of lakes
  int<lower=0> y[J]; // number of pilots from elodea-infested sources into lake j
  int<lower=0> n[J]; // number of total pilots that fly into lake j (number of trials)
}
parameters {
  real<lower=0,upper=1> theta[J]; // chances of success: a pilot originating from an elodea-infested source destined for j
  real<lower=0,upper=1> lambda; // prior mean chance of success
  real<lower=0.1> kappa; // prior count
}
transformed parameters {
  real<lower=0> alpha; // prior success count
  real<lower=0> beta; // prior failure count
  alpha = lambda* kappa;
  beta =   (1 - lambda)* kappa;
}
model {
  lambda ~ uniform(0,1); // hyperprior
  kappa ~ uniform(0.1,5); // hyperprior 
  theta ~ beta(alpha,beta); // prior
  y ~ binomial(n,theta); // likelihood
}
generated quantities {
  real<lower=0,upper=1> avg; // avg success
  int<lower=0,upper=1> above_avg[J]; // true if j is above avg
  int<lower=1,upper=J> rnk[J]; // rank of j
  int<lower=0,upper=1> highest[J]; // true if j is highest rank
  avg = mean(theta);
    for (j in 1:J)
    above_avg[j] = (theta[j] > avg);
    for (j in 1:J) {
    rnk[j] = rank(theta,j) + 1;
    highest[j] = rnk[j] == 1;
  }
}
